claims.text: 3D ink-extrusion printing is applicable to AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock.
3D ink-extrusion printing can manufacture miniature metallic components from powder-containing inks.
3D ink-extrusion printing imposes a lower thermal load than mainstream metallic additive-manufacturing regimes.
AlCrFeNiSi ink-extrusion printing can be performed under room-temperature processing conditions.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing produces problematic residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi components.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing degrades the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi components.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing entails problematic processing complexity for AlCrFeNiSi components.
Low-thermal-load ink-extrusion printing refines the microstructure of AlCrFeNiSi.
Low-thermal-load ink-extrusion printing reduces thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi.
The reduced thermal load causes both microstructure refinement and lower residual stress.
Relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing, ink-extrusion printing improves the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi components.
Relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing, ink-extrusion printing reduces residual stress in AlCrFeNiSi components.
Ink-extrusion printing makes processing simpler than conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing.
The proposed intervention is limited to AlCrFeNiSi powder feedstock processed by 3D ink extrusion.
